subject: maths
title: Year 6 Simplifying and Comparing Fractions
seo_title: Year 6 Simplifying and Comparing Fractions Worksheets: Simplest Form, Mixed Numbers, Ordering (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Use common factors to simplify fractions; use common multiples to express fractions in the same denomination; compare and order fractions, including fractions > 1.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on simplifying and comparing fractions for the National Curriculum: simplest form with the highest common factor, improper fractions and mixed numbers, common denominators, ordering fractions greater than 1 and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Simplify by dividing by the highest common factor. Compare by giving the fractions a common denominator.
key_sub: 18/24 = 3/4 (÷ 6). 2/3 and 3/4 become 8/12 and 9/12, so 3/4 is greater. A bigger denominator means smaller parts.
body_html:
Simplifying fractions

A fraction is in its simplest form when the numerator and the denominator have no common factor except 1. To simplify, divide both numbers by their highest common factor (HCF). The value does not change.

Example

Write 1824 in its simplest form.

Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The HCF is 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

Answer: 34

If you divide by a smaller common factor, such as 2, you get 912. That is correct but not finished: keep going until there is no common factor left.

Improper fractions and mixed numbers

An improper fraction such as 74 is greater than 1. A mixed number such as 1 34 shows the same amount as wholes and a fraction.

Example

Write 175 as a mixed number.

5 goes into 17 three times (15), with 2 left over.

Answer: 3 25

Example

Write 2 35 as an improper fraction.

2 wholes = 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Add 3 fifths: 10 + 3 = 13.

Answer: 135

Common denominators

To compare fractions with different denominators, give them the same denominator. Use the lowest common multiple (LCM) of the denominators.

Example

Write 23 and 34 with a common denominator.

The LCM of 3 and 4 is 12. 23 = 812 (× 4) and 34 = 912 (× 3).

Answer: 812 and 912

Comparing and ordering

Once the denominators are the same, compare the numerators. For numbers greater than 1, compare the wholes first, then the fractions.

Example

Which is greater: 54 or 1 13?

Both are 1 and a bit. Compare 14 and 13 using twelfths: 312 < 412.

Answer: 1 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking the same number away from the top and bottom: 2030 → 1020Divide both by the HCF: 2030 = 23
Thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction: 18 > 16A bigger denominator means smaller parts: 18 < 16
Comparing only the numerators: 49 > 35 because 4 > 3Use a common denominator: 2045 < 2745
2 35 = 65 (multiplying 2 × 3)Wholes × denominator, then add the numerator: 2 × 5 + 3 = 13, so 135

faq.q: How do you simplify fractions in Year 6?
faq.a: Find the highest common factor of the numerator and denominator, then divide both by it. For 18/24 the highest common factor is 6, so 18/24 = 3/4.

faq.q: How do you compare fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Write them with a common denominator, using the lowest common multiple of the denominators, then compare the numerators. For 2/3 and 3/4, use twelfths: 8/12 is less than 9/12.

faq.q: What is the difference between an improper fraction and a mixed number?
faq.a: An improper fraction has a numerator bigger than (or equal to) its denominator, such as 7/4. A mixed number shows the same amount as wholes and a fraction, such as 1 3/4.

faq.q: Are fractions in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. Fractions appear in the arithmetic paper and in both reasoning papers, including simplifying, comparing and ordering fractions and solving word problems with them.

sets.title: Simplify fractions using the highest common factor

items.q: 68 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 2. Write 68 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 4 groups and 3 of them are shaded, so 68 = 34. This is the same as dividing 6 and 8 by 2.

items.q: 410 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 2. Write 410 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 5 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 410 = 25. This is the same as dividing 4 and 10 by 2.

items.q: 69 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 3. Write 69 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 3 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 69 = 23. This is the same as dividing 6 and 9 by 3.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 18 and 24?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, and the highest is 6.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 12 and 30?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, and the highest is 6.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 16 and 40?
items.e: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The common factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, and the highest is 8.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 27 and 36?
items.e: Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The common factors are 1, 3, 9, and the highest is 9.

items.q: Write 1824 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 18 and 24 is 6. Divide both numbers by 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. So 1824 = 34. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 1216 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 12 and 16 is 4. Divide both numbers by 4: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 16 ÷ 4 = 4. So 1216 = 34. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 1520 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 15 and 20 is 5. Divide both numbers by 5: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. So 1520 = 34. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 1025 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 10 and 25 is 5. Divide both numbers by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 25 ÷ 5 = 5. So 1025 = 25. 2 and 5 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 1421 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 14 and 21 is 7. Divide both numbers by 7: 14 ÷ 7 = 2 and 21 ÷ 7 = 3. So 1421 = 23. 2 and 3 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 2436 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12. Divide both numbers by 12: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3. So 2436 = 23. 2 and 3 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 1640 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 16 and 40 is 8. Divide both numbers by 8: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 and 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 1640 = 25. 2 and 5 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 2128 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 21 and 28 is 7. Divide both numbers by 7: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. So 2128 = 34. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 3045 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 30 and 45 is 15. Divide both numbers by 15: 30 ÷ 15 = 2 and 45 ÷ 15 = 3. So 3045 = 23. 2 and 3 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 2012 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 20 and 12 is 4. Divide both numbers by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 2012 = 53. 5 and 3 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified. (It is still more than 1, so the numerator stays bigger than the denominator.)

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 5 and 8 have no common factor except 1, so 58 is in its simplest form. The others can be simplified: 69 = 23 (÷ 3); 410 = 25 (÷ 2); 912 = 34 (÷ 3).

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 7 and 12 have no common factor except 1, so 712 is in its simplest form. The others can be simplified: 814 = 47 (÷ 2); 1015 = 23 (÷ 5); 39 = 13 (÷ 3).

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 9 and 16 have no common factor except 1, so 916 is in its simplest form. The others can be simplified: 614 = 37 (÷ 2); 1525 = 35 (÷ 5); 1222 = 611 (÷ 2).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full and 3 more parts are shaded in the last bar. So it shows 114 = 2 34.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full and 1 more part is shaded in the last bar. So it shows 73 = 2 13.

items.q: Write 175 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 5s go into 17? 3 × 5 = 15, so there are 3 wholes. 17 − 15 = 2 are left over. So 175 = 3 25.

items.q: Write 114 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 4s go into 11? 2 × 4 = 8, so there are 2 wholes. 11 − 8 = 3 are left over. So 114 = 2 34.

items.q: Write 236 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 6s go into 23? 3 × 6 = 18, so there are 3 wholes. 23 − 18 = 5 are left over. So 236 = 3 56.

items.q: Write 198 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 8s go into 19? 2 × 8 = 16, so there are 2 wholes. 19 − 16 = 3 are left over. So 198 = 2 38.

items.q: Write 2910 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 10s go into 29? 2 × 10 = 20, so there are 2 wholes. 29 − 20 = 9 are left over. So 2910 = 2 910.

items.q: Write 133 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 3s go into 13? 4 × 3 = 12, so there are 4 wholes. 13 − 12 = 1 is left over. So 133 = 4 13.

items.q: Write 317 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 7s go into 31? 4 × 7 = 28, so there are 4 wholes. 31 − 28 = 3 are left over. So 317 = 4 37.

items.q: Write 144 as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: How many 4s go into 14? 3 × 4 = 12, so there are 3 wholes. 14 − 12 = 2 are left over. So 144 = 3 24. Simplify the fraction part: 24 = 12 (÷ 2). So the answer is 3 12.

items.q: Write 228 as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: How many 8s go into 22? 2 × 8 = 16, so there are 2 wholes. 22 − 16 = 6 are left over. So 228 = 2 68. Simplify the fraction part: 68 = 34 (÷ 2). So the answer is 2 34.

items.q: Write 2 35 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 55, so 2 wholes are 2 × 5 = 10 parts. Add the 3: 10 + 3 = 13. So 2 35 = 135.

items.q: Write 3 14 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 44, so 3 wholes are 3 × 4 = 12 parts. Add the 1: 12 + 1 = 13. So 3 14 = 134.

items.q: Write 4 23 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 33, so 4 wholes are 4 × 3 = 12 parts. Add the 2: 12 + 2 = 14. So 4 23 = 143.

items.q: Write 5 38 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 88, so 5 wholes are 5 × 8 = 40 parts. Add the 3: 40 + 3 = 43. So 5 38 = 438.

items.q: Write 2 710 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 1010, so 2 wholes are 2 × 10 = 20 parts. Add the 7: 20 + 7 = 27. So 2 710 = 2710.

items.q: Write 6 12 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 22, so 6 wholes are 6 × 2 = 12 parts. Add the 1: 12 + 1 = 13. So 6 12 = 132.

items.q: Write 3 56 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 66, so 3 wholes are 3 × 6 = 18 parts. Add the 5: 18 + 5 = 23. So 3 56 = 236.

items.q: 3 14 = ?4
items.e: 3 wholes = 3 × 4 = 12 quarters. Add 1 more quarter: 12 + 1 = 13. So 3 14 = 134.

items.q: 478 = ? 78
items.e: 8 × 5 = 40 and 47 − 40 = 7. So 478 = 5 78.

sets.title: Write fractions with a common denominator

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 4 and 6?
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, … Multiples of 6: 6, 12, … The first number in both lists is 12. 4 × 6 = 24 is a common multiple too, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 6 and 8?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, … Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, … The first number in both lists is 24. 6 × 8 = 48 is a common multiple too, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 3 and 5?
items.e: Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, … Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, … The first number in both lists is 15.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 9 and 12?
items.e: Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, … Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, … The first number in both lists is 36. 9 × 12 = 108 is a common multiple too, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: 35 = ?20
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. So 35 = 1220.

items.q: 23 = ?12
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 = 812.

items.q: 56 = ?18
items.e: 6 × 3 = 18, so multiply the numerator by 3 too: 5 × 3 = 15. So 56 = 1518.

items.q: 78 = ?24
items.e: 8 × 3 = 24, so multiply the numerator by 3 too: 7 × 3 = 21. So 78 = 2124.

items.q: 49 = ?36
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16. So 49 = 1636.

items.q: 34 = 15?
items.e: 3 × 5 = 15, so multiply the denominator by 5 too: 4 × 5 = 20. So 34 = 1520.

items.q: Write 23 and 34 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 912 and 812
612 and 1212
212 and 312
812 and 912
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 23 = 812 (× 4); 34 = 912 (× 3). Answer: 812 and 912.

items.q: Write 12 and 35 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 510 and 610
110 and 310
910 and 810
210 and 1510
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 2 and 5 is 10, so use 10 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 12 = 510 (× 5); 35 = 610 (× 2). Answer: 510 and 610.

items.q: Write 34 and 56 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 312 and 512
1012 and 912
612 and 1512
912 and 1012
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so use 12 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 34 = 912 (× 3); 56 = 1012 (× 2). Answer: 912 and 1012.

items.q: Write 13 and 512 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 112 and 2012
112 and 512
412 and 512
1012 and 512
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 12 is 12, so use 12 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 13 = 412 (× 4); 512 stays 512. Answer: 412 and 512.

items.q: Write 56 and 79 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 1518 and 1418
518 and 718
1718 and 1618
1018 and 2118
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 6 and 9 is 18, so use 18 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 56 = 1518 (× 3); 79 = 1418 (× 2). Answer: 1518 and 1418.

items.q: Write 38 and 16 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 324 and 124
924 and 424
1224 and 324
424 and 924
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 8 and 6 is 24, so use 24 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 38 = 924 (× 3); 16 = 424 (× 4). Answer: 924 and 424.

items.q: Write 25 and 310 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 410 and 310
710 and 310
210 and 310
210 and 610
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 10 is 10, so use 10 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 25 = 410 (× 2); 310 stays 310. Answer: 410 and 310.

items.q: Which number could be a common denominator for 14 and 16?
items.e: A common denominator must be in the 4 times table and the 6 times table. 12 = 4 × 3 = 6 × 2. 10 is the sum of 4 and 6, which does not work.

items.q: Which number could be a common denominator for 13 and 18?
items.e: A common denominator must be in the 3 times table and the 8 times table. 24 = 3 × 8 = 8 × 3. 11 is the sum of 3 and 8, which does not work.

items.q: Which number could be a common denominator for 15 and 14?
items.e: A common denominator must be in the 5 times table and the 4 times table. 20 = 5 × 4 = 4 × 5. 9 is the sum of 5 and 4, which does not work.

sets.title: Compare and order fractions, including fractions greater than 1

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 23?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. Count 1 whole, then 2 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 14?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. Count 2 wholes, then 1 more mark. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 75?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 75 = 1 25: go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 116?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 116 = 1 56: go to 1, then 5 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 24: 34 = 1824, 58 = 1524, 23 = 1624, 712 = 1424. The greatest is 1824, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 36: 56 = 3036, 79 = 2836, 34 = 2736, 23 = 2436. The smallest is 2436, so the answer is 23.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 24: 512 = 1024, 38 = 924, 13 = 824, 724 = 724. The smallest is 724, so the answer is 724.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All four are between 1 and 2. Look at how much each one is short of 2: 74 = 1 34 (14 short), 1 23 (13 short), 95 = 1 45 (15 short), 1 58 (38 short). The smallest gap is 15, so 95 is the greatest.

items.q: Which fraction is between 12 and 34?
items.e: In eighths: 12 = 48 and 34 = 68. 58 is between them. 78 and 45 are more than 34, and 38 is less than 12.

items.q:

items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 23 = 812, 56 = 1012, 712 = 712. So the order is 712, 23, 56.

items.q:

items.e: Use the common denominator 10: 35 = 610, 12 = 510, 710 = 710. So the order is 12, 35, 710.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:

c: 1 13, 32, 54
32, 54, 1 13
32, 1 13, 54
54, 1 13, 32
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 32 = 1812, 54 = 1512, 1 13 = 1612. So the order is 54, 1 13, 32.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:

c: 94, 136, 2 13
136, 94, 2 13
94, 2 13, 136
2 13, 94, 136
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 94 = 2712, 2 13 = 2812, 136 = 2612. So the order is 136, 94, 2 13.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: 49 > 35
23 = 34
54 < 1 13
18 > 16
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 54 = 1512 and 1 13 = 1612. So 54 < 1 13 is true.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: 78 > 56
310 > 37
35 = 46
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 78 = 2124 and 56 = 2024. So 78 > 56 is true.

items.q: Which statement is true?

35 < 58

29 > 25
items.e: Use the common denominator 40: 35 = 2440 and 58 = 2540. So 35 < 58 is true.

items.q: Which statement is true?

118 > 1 12
512 > 58
2 25 > 94
items.e: Use the common denominator 20: 2 25 = 4820 and 94 = 4520. So 2 25 > 94 is true.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: 52 < 2 14
710 > 56
46 = 1015
611 > 45
items.e: Simplify both: 46 = 23 (÷ 2) and 1015 = 23 (÷ 5). They are equal, so 46 = 1015 is true.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: 116 < 1 78
712 < 12
94 = 34
57 > 34
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 116 = 4424 and 1 78 = 4524. So 116 < 1 78 is true.

items.q: Oliver eats 38 of a pizza. Amelia eats 13 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Use 24ths: 38 = 924 and 13 = 824. 9 is more than 8, so Oliver eats more.

items.q: In Class 6A, 18 of the 30 pupils bring a packed lunch. In Class 6B, 14 of the 20 pupils bring a packed lunch. Which class has the greater fraction of pupils with a packed lunch?
items.e: Class 6A: 1830 = 35 = 610. Class 6B: 1420 = 710. 710 is more than 610, so Class 6B. Class 6A has more pupils, but a smaller fraction of them.

items.q: 24 of the 32 pupils in Year 6 went on the school trip. What fraction of the pupils went? Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The fraction is 2432. The highest common factor of 24 and 32 is 8: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 32 ÷ 8 = 4. So 34 of the pupils went.

items.q: Flour comes in bags of 14 kg. How many bags make 2 34 kg?
items.e: Each whole kilogram is 4 bags, so 2 kg is 2 × 4 = 8 bags. Add 3 more bags for 34 kg: 8 + 3 = 11 bags. (2 34 = 114.)

items.q: Harry runs 134 km. Write this distance as a mixed number.
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12 and 13 − 12 = 1. So 134 km = 3 14 km.

items.q: Four children measure their ribbons. Isla: 56 m. Jack: 79 m. Poppy: 34 m. Arjun: 23 m. Who has the longest ribbon?
items.e: Use the common denominator 36: 56 = 3036, 79 = 2836, 34 = 2736, 23 = 2436. The longest is Isla’s.

items.q: Bottle A holds 1 14 litres of water. Bottle B holds 75 litres. Which bottle holds more?
items.e: 75 = 1 25. Compare 14 and 25 using twentieths: 520 and 820. So Bottle B holds more.

items.q: Ruby says, “49 is greater than 35, because 4 is greater than 3.” Is she right?
c: No. 49 is less than 35
Yes. Ninths are bigger than fifths
items.e: You cannot compare only the numerators when the denominators are different. Use 45ths: 49 = 2045 and 35 = 2745. So 49 is less than 35.

items.q: Ethan simplified 2030 and wrote 1020. What did he do wrong?
c: He divided by the highest common factor
He took 10 away from the top and the bottom
He divided only the numerator by 2
items.e: 20 − 10 = 10 and 30 − 10 = 20. Subtracting changes the value: 1020 = 12, not 23. Divide by the highest common factor, 10: 2030 = 23.

items.q: Kai says 3 25 = 65. What is the correct improper fraction?
items.e: Kai multiplied 3 × 2. Instead, 3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: The Reds football team won 7 of their 12 matches. The Blues won 5 of their 8 matches. Which team won the greater fraction of their matches?
items.e: Use 24ths: Reds 712 = 1424, Blues 58 = 1524. 15 is more than 14, so the Blues. The Reds won more matches, but they also played more.

items.q: Lily lives 1 12 km from school, George 74 km, Maya 1 25 km and Zara 1 35 km. Who lives furthest from school?
items.e: 74 = 1 34. Compare the fraction parts with the denominator 20: 12 = 1020, 34 = 1520, 25 = 820, 35 = 1220. The largest is 1520, so George lives furthest.

items.q: There are 36 pupils on a coach. 27 of them are in Year 6. What fraction of the pupils are in Year 6, in its simplest form?
items.e: The fraction is 2736. The highest common factor of 27 and 36 is 9: 27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 36 ÷ 9 = 4. So 34.

items.q: Two cakes are each cut into 12 equal slices. 15 slices are eaten. How many cakes are eaten? Give a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: 15 slices = 1512 cakes. 12 slices make 1 whole cake and 3 are left: 1 312. Simplify: 312 = 14 (÷ 3). So 1 14 cakes.

items.q: Charlie reads for 56 of an hour. Evie reads for 34 of an hour. Who reads for longer?
c: They read for the same time
items.e: Use 12ths: 56 = 1012 and 34 = 912, so Charlie reads for longer. (In minutes: 50 minutes and 45 minutes.)

items.q: Freya and Leo get the same pocket money. Freya spends 38 of hers and Leo spends 25 of his. Who spends more?
items.e: Use 40ths: 38 = 1540 and 25 = 1640. 16 is more than 15, so Leo spends more.

items.q: In a spelling test, Mohammed scores 16 out of 20 and Aisha scores 21 out of 25. Who did better?
c: Aisha, because 2125 = 84100 and 1620 = 80100
They did the same, because both lost 4 or 5 marks
Mohammed, because 1620 = 45
items.e: Write both out of 100: 1620 = 80100 (× 5) and 2125 = 84100 (× 4). 84 is more than 80, so Aisha did better.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. At a party, 19 slices of the same-sized pizzas are eaten. How many pizzas is that?
items.e: 6 slices make 1 pizza. 3 × 6 = 18, and 19 − 18 = 1 slice is left. So 196 = 3 16 pizzas.

items.q: Arjun eats 14 of a cake. Zara eats 16 of the same cake. He writes both fractions as twelfths to compare them. What should he write?
c: 212 and 312
412 and 612
112 and 112
312 and 212
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12, so 14 = 312. 6 × 2 = 12, so 16 = 212. Answer: 312 and 212. Arjun eats more.

items.q: In Class 6R, 12 of the 28 pupils walk to school. In Class 6T, 9 of the 21 pupils walk to school. Which class has the greater fraction of pupils who walk?
items.e: Simplify both. 1228 = 37 (÷ 4) and 921 = 37 (÷ 3). The fractions are equal, so they are the same.
